title: sealedsecret: safe-swap flow with kms fallback, probe job, and recovery playbooks
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Introduce a staged SealedSecret rotation flow with automatic fallback to KMS-wrapped values, pre-upgrade probes and documented recovery playbooks. No user-visible API changes.
description: Motivation: private deployments that use SealedSecrets + Vault/KMS face a race during TLS/KMS key rotations where consumers may receive partially-rotated secrets. This PR implements a safe 'swap' flow to allow staged SealedSecret rotation with an automated compatibility probe and a documented rollback/recovery path. Goals: 1) perform TLS/KMS-based rotation with zero-secret-latency windows for runtime; 2) detect keywrap/unwrap incompatibilities prior to cutover; 3) provide easy rollback and audit telemetry for operators. Changes are split across Helm templates, Helm hooks, a small controller-ish job for probing previously-rotated entries, Terraform variables for the installer, and runbooks/playbooks for operators. Checklist: - [x] Helm chart: new values for sealedsecret.swap.enabled, probeJob config, and pre-upgrade hook annotations - [x] Helm templates: introduce sealedsecret-safe-swap Job and associated RBAC - [x] Terraform: optional var enable_sealedsecret_safe_swap and minimal IAM/KMS policy docs - [x] Installer hooks: pre-upgrade probe step and post-failback cleanup - [x] Recovery playbooks: operator runbook for canary, rollback, and forced rewrap - [x] E2E smoke test added to ci/upgrade-tests that exercises probe job against a simulated KMS mismatch - [x] CI: new pipeline step added to run the probe job in the chart verification job Rationale/flow: 1) Deploy new chart with sealedsecret.swap.enabled=true; the chart installs a probe Job (disabled by default) and adds annotations to SealedSecrets managed by the installer to include a rotation metadata label. 2) Operator triggers rotation; the system creates rewrapped SealedSecret objects under a staging suffix and the probe Job attempts to unwrap them using the target KMS key material. 3) If all probe unwrappings succeed, a safe-swap controller (lightweight K8s Job run by Helm hook) performs an atomic replace of the live secrets; otherwise the probe returns detailed failure reasons and the installer can either rollback or continue to manual remediation. 4) If a failure occurs after partial cutover, recovery playbooks provide steps to: rewrap to prior key, promote canary nodes to traffic, and audit the event using the new telemetry labels. Telemetry: chart adds labels and emits events to the installer operator (via the probe Job logs) with structured messages that the Console can pick up (rotation.id=<uuid>, stage=probe|commit|rollback, failures=...). Security considerations: the probe Job has least-privilege IAM/KMS usage documented; secrets are never written to disk unencrypted and logs redact key material. Implementation notes: - The probe job is implemented as a small Go binary (probe-wrap-check) compiled into an image referenced in values.yaml. It performs KMS Unwrap in a dry-run mode and returns deterministic status codes. - Helm templates add a pre-upgrade hook that can be toggled off (useful for low-trust air-gapped upgrades). - Terraform variables add optional IAM role binding for probe job when enable_sealedsecret_safe_swap=true. Migration notes: existing installations must opt-in by setting values.sealedsecret.swap.enabled=true; default remains off to avoid surprising behavior. See docs/private-deployments/sealedsecret-safe-swap.md for operator guidance and playbooks.

notes_for_ops: Operators: to enable the safe-swap flow, set charts.private-installer.sealedsecret.swap.enabled=true and ensure the installer has a kms:Decrypt IAM role bound to the probe SA. Use the included playbook 'sealedsecret-safe-swap.md' before scheduling a rotation. If the probe reports 'unwrap-failure: key-version-mismatch', run 'installer sealedsecret rewrap --from <old-key> --to <new-key> --rotation <id>' to reconcile, then re-run the probe. Audit: rotation events include rotation.id label for correlation.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfigured KMS IAM could cause probe to fail and block automated cutover. Mitigation: probe is opt-in and chart will not alter live secrets until probe passes; there is a documented operator rollback path and automated cleanup hook.
